subject: Post-call: SLO & deployment qualification for Polaris Health — next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Thank you — call recap & next steps (SLOs / topology)

Thanks Emily and Rajiv — good conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track decisions.

Pain points you described:
- End-user summaries (single-turn) must feel instantaneous: target ~120ms p95 end-to-end for the summary endpoint.
- Multi-turn clinical chat can tolerate higher latency but must be available for spikes during business hours (40–100 req/s).
- PHI-sensitive workload: Polaris needs VPC/private deployment, KMS/HSM for keys, and a BA agreement in place.
- Predictable cost and a clear fallback plan if the primary cluster is under heavy load.

What we heard as goals:
1) Deploy a production-grade inference stack in your AWS us-east-1 VPC (private control plane).
2) Meet ~120ms p95 for single-turn summaries and keep multi-turn p95 < 300ms.
3) Handle steady-state throughput of ~50–80 req/s with short bursts to ~120 req/s.
4) End-to-end observability (token + request-level cost, latency breakdowns, alerts).

High-level technical notes / model constraints:
- Preferred model class: 7B–13B fine-tuned conversational model (you mentioned a recent internal finetune).
- Recommended quantization: 4-bit (Q4) using our validated kernels to balance latency and quality.
- We’ll use prefix/KV caching for templated prompts to reduce per-request compute.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Marissa (cc'd) will share a short SLO proposal and a topology diagram (target: tomorrow EOD).
- Emily/Rajiv: please share the completed security questionnaire and an expected monthly request profile (hourly buckets preferable).
- I’ll schedule a procurement/finance intro and share a preliminary commercial outline.

Attachments: I referenced a short template SOW and will attach a draft SLO workbook once Marissa confirms numbers.

Thanks — speak soon.

--

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A couple clarifications from our side so your SRE/SE teams can size correctly:
- Our strict requirement is 120ms p95 for single-turn clinical summary requests (typical prompt lengths ~150 tokens).
- Multi-turn clinical assistant: target p95 250–300ms; some conversations will be 8–12 turns.
- Traffic shape: business hours 08:00–18:00 ET have 40–100 req/s (peaks around 10:30 and 15:00), overnight is <10 req/s.
- Deployment: we require a private deployment inside our AWS account (us-east-1), with the option to move to an on-prem appliance if needed for some clinics.

I attached the completed security questionnaire (Polaris-security-questionnaire_v2.xlsx). Also can you provide a ballpark monthly cost range and a timeline for a pilot (2–3 weeks) vs. production? Procurement will want those numbers up front.

Subject: SLO proposal + deployment topology (draft)

Hi Emily — thanks for the data points. Attached is a short SLO workbook and a proposed deployment topology (polaris-slo-proposal.xlsx). Below is an executive summary of the technical recommendations and the expected performance envelope based on Polaris's traffic profile.

Executive summary (recommendation):
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated cluster inside Polaris VPC (Private control plane).
  - Base nodes: 2 x A100-80GB dedicated GPUs for inference (serving cluster).
  - Autoscaling: Add 1 node at 60% sustained util, add up to +2 nodes for bursts (fast scale-up window = 30s).
  - Canary/fallback: Hosted smaller model (7B distilled variant) in our hosted tier to route <10% of traffic during heavy overloads.

- Model & runtime: Llama2-13B fine-tuned (candidate) — quantized to Q4; uses FlashAttention/optimized kernels.
  - KV/prefix caching enabled for templated summary prompts to avoid re-encoding static context.
  - Dynamic batching target: batch size 6–8 (configurable by request latency budget).

- Expected latency (benchmarks based on similar workloads):
  - Cold-start (container spin+warmup): ~1.5–3.0s (first request after scale event).
  - Steady-state token latency: ~6–10ms/token p95 on A100-80GB with Q4 kernels.
  - Single-turn end-to-end p95 (150-token prompt + 60-token completion): ~110–140ms (includes network hop inside VPC + runtime).
  - Multi-turn p95 (with KV cache warm): ~200–280ms depending on history length and completion size.

- Throughput expectations:
  - With two GPUs and the batching strategy above: sustainable ~80–120 req/s for single-turn workloads (short completions).
  - Autoscaling policy handles bursts to ~220 req/s for short periods (queueing + drop-in fallback).

- Observability & SLO enforcement:
  - Token-level latency breakdown, per-route cost, and SLA alerts (email + PagerDuty) included.
  - Canary rollout option: 5% traffic for 48 hours before widening.

- Security / compliance:
  - SOC 2 + HIPAA controls available in Private plan.
  - KMS/HSM key management integration + audit logs.

Proposed pilot (2 weeks):
1) Week 1: Provision Dedicated cluster in a test VPC, run synthetic load to validate p95 numbers and tuning (batch size, kernel selection).
2) Week 2: Shadow traffic with real requests (no user impact), measure quality + latency, adjust autoscaler and caching.

Cost & timeline (rough):
- Pilot: 2-week engineering support + Dedicated infra (estimate range $25k–$45k depending on GPU reservation model).
- Prod: Monthly committed capacity pricing to be finalized after pilot; initial reserved commit for the two-node baseline recommended.

Attachments: polaris-slo-proposal.xlsx (SLO workbook + topology diagram).

Next technical actions I need from Polaris:
- Confirm exact model artifact (if you have an internal fine-tune we can benchmark that image).
- Provide a short sample prompt set (5–10 canonical prompts) and a representative traffic CSV (hourly buckets).

If this looks OK I'll convert the workbook to a formal SOW draft and coordinate procurement language with Karthik.

Best,
